## Abstract

We give an alternative proof of a point-process version of the FKG–Holley–Preston inequality which provides a sufficient condition for stochastic domination of probability measures, and for positive correlations of increasing functions.

## 🏷️ Why exact centering matters

An error tending to zero in the law of large numbers need not disappear after multiplication by μ ε​​=ε−1. An order-ε correction to the mean becomes an order-one shift at the fluctuation scale.

The companion computes precisely such an excluded-volume correction at time zero. Thus replacing the exact microscopic expectation by ∫f t​ϕ would generally change the limiting mean. This is a useful lesson whenever a central limit theorem is built on a deterministic limit: the centering requires a sharper estimate than convergence alone.

Random particle number also changes the initial covariance. The stated limit is

E[ζ 0​(ϕ)ζ 0​(ψ)]=∫f 0​ϕ ψ.

There is no fixed-sample-size subtraction of (∫f 0​ϕ)(∫f 0​ψ). For a Poisson sum, the fluctuation in the number of summands contributes exactly the term that would otherwise be subtracted.

## 🏷️ Retaining correlations across time layers

One cannot repeatedly restart a short-time chaos theorem as though the particles were independent at each restart. Thus the final sum of records equals the chosen linear combination of all observations exactly.

In the limiting expansion, F t​ is the one-root marked law and J t​ the two-root connected law. Deleting the last collision of a tree splits it into two components. This identifies their evolution with the Boltzmann equation and its linearization. The full covariance also contains the same-particle contribution:

G t​(Φ,Ψ)=J t​(Φ⊗Ψ)+F t​(ΦΨ).

Restoring this diagonal term and using pre/postcollision symmetry produces the covariance source with products of collision increments Δ ϕ=ϕ′+ϕ∗′​−ϕ−ϕ∗​. Higher connected cumulants vanish at the fluctuation normalization; the surviving first two cumulants determine the Gaussian limit. These conclusions require the source’s sharp tree bounds and spatial disintegration estimates, which justify multiplying component measures at a common position.

### Exact centering requires more than a likely coupling

Let E ε​ be the event on which the true and restarted trajectories differ. The manuscript proves P(E ε​)=O(ε 1+η). For a bounded record sum S, the difference is at most 2 M obs​N 1 E ε​​. Hölder’s inequality and bounded normalized particle-number moments give

μ​∣E S true−E S restart∣​≤C p​ε−1+(1+η)(1−1/p).

Choose p>(1+η)/η so the exponent is positive. The expectation difference is then negligible at the fluctuation scale. Agreement with probability tending to one would suffice for uncentered differences in probability, but not for this expectation comparison. This final estimate transfers the Gaussian law with its exact microscopic centering. # The hard sphere gas in the Boltzmann-Grad limit

https://doi.org/10.1016/0378-4371(81)90207-7Get rights and content

## Abstract

This talk will review what has been rigorously proved about the time-dependent behaviour of a gas of classical hard spheres in the limiting regime where the number n of particles per unit volume becomes infinitely large while the particle diameter ϵ goes to zero in such a way that nϵ^{2} approaches a finite non-zero limit. (It is in this limiting regime that the Boltzmann equation is expected to become exact.)

The review will emphasize general conceptual issues including: (1) How one constructs, in a mathematically precise way, a reduced macroscopic description appropriate to this limiting regime. (2) How probabilistic considerations enter the analysis. (3) At what point irreversibility appears.

## Résumé

Dans cette communication, on examine ce qui a été démontré rigoureusement pour le comportement dépendant du temps d'un gaz classique de sphéres dures, dans le régime limite où le nombre n de particules par unité de volume devient infiniment grand, alors que le diamètre ϵ des particules tend vers zéro de façon que nϵ^{2} se rapproche d'une limite finie non nulle. (C'est dans ce régime limite qu'on s'attend à ce que l'équation de Boltzmann devienne exacte.)

En faisant cette revue, on insistera sur les problèmes conceptuels généraux, entre autres: (1) Comment construire, d'une façon mathématiquement précise, une description macroscopique réduite appropriée au régime limite en question. (2) Ce quelle façon les considérations probabilistes intervienent dans l'analyse. (3) A quel point apparaît l'irréversibilité.

Title: One-sided convergence in the Boltzmann-Grad limit
Authors: Thierry Bodineau, Isabelle Gallagher, Laure Saint-Raymond, Sergio Simonella
Date: Mon Dec 12 14:52:22 2016

We review various contributions on the fundamental work of Lanford deriving the Boltzmann equation from hard-sphere dynamics in the low density limit. We focus especially on the assumptions made on the initial data and on how they encode irreversibility. The impossibility to reverse time in the Boltzmann equation (expressed for instance by Boltzmann's H-theorem) is related to the lack of convergence of higher order marginals on some singular sets. Explicit counterexamples single out the microscopic sets where the initial data should converge in order to produce the Boltzmann dynamics.--------------------------------------------------------------------------------
